item.title: Frickin' LAZER BEAMS!
item.description: Norway now has more than 2,000 underwater AI laser robots shooting lice off its salmon. They're made by a company called Stingray, and they already guard more than 50 million salmon and trout 24/7. The reason is sea lice, tiny parasites that latch onto salmon and feed on them. As few as 11 can kill a small fish, and one pen can hold 150,000 salmon. The usual fix is pumping the fish out and blasting them with warm water or water jets to knock the lice off. The handling is so rough that Norway's fish health report ranks it the top cause of death in full-grown farmed salmon. So instead, Stingray puts a robot inside the pen that hunts lice one at a time, all day: > two cameras watch every salmon that swims past > AI checks two frames to make sure it's really a louse > then a green laser fires from up to 2 meters away > the salmon's scales reflect the beam, so the fish swims off fine and the louse is dead We now live in a world where AI lasers do pest control on your dinner.

item.title: They are going to be together forever!!!
item.description:
A random Imgurian from CO messaged me a couple of months ago because she was interested in adopting foster kitten Lucky Day. I was super stoked. We chatted for a while, and got plans together for her trip to AL.
I sent her videos of Lucky with his brothers, specifically the times he tussled with brother Dusty Bottoms. I jokingly said she should take both. I mean, she’s already flying all the way here, may as well take two, right?
And she agreed!!! Lucky and Dusty have found their forever home!
My friend Rich was super interested in the third amigo, Ned. I was planning to take all three to his house on Wednesday to meet his current cat, one of my old fosters Joey from the Friends litter! I was hoping the two would hit it off. Ned gets along with everyone.
But his son decided he wants a black kitten. Dangit. I’ll be on the lookout for a good void for you, Drew!
They’re all super cute and wonderful. And everyone and their mom have been telling me how awesome it would be if they were all adopted together. Ned will be fine by himself, I truly believe that. But I had a drink (or two) tonight and gave the CO Imgurian a call and said I would be ok if she wanted to adopt all three…and…
She and her husband agreed!!!
They have plane tickets!! And carriers!!! And it’s HAPPENING!! The Three Amigos are being adopted TOGETHER!!!

item.title: I take some blame
item.description: I just looked at an old post of mine from early 2025 and it had around 3k upvotes. These days seeing a post get over 1000 upvotes feels rare. A while ago I made an image that said "Fuck you, business daddy," and had PhotoShopped the MediaLab logo into a screenshot from Last Week Tonight with John Oliver and the Imgur logo onto Mr. Oliver. On August 25th of 2025 that image became a unifying rallying cry of protest towards the parent company MediaLab and the enshitification of Imgur. The catalyst for this protest was the Notification feature not working for a number of days. I believe that many Imgurians saw this as the point of no return for the site and many left immediately after this event. Since then the numbers have continued to dwindle. Anyways, thought this was an appropriate confession bear. Be careful what you Photoshop. FP Edit: Trans Rights Are Human Rights

item.title: I Became Arm Candy at a CEO Party…
item.description: I've had some really wonderful conversations with folks here after sharing my last couple of videos, so I wanted to share another experience that I think some of you might relate to. I recently went on a date in Las Vegas that ended with me in that fancy gold dress at an exclusive CEO party. Except this time, instead of navigating the room as one of the guys like I used to, I was the arm candy. It brought up some surprisingly complicated feelings about femininity, gender euphoria, and even how experiencing everyday misogyny can sometimes feel weirdly affirming as a trans woman. My friend joined me to unpack the experience and talk about some of the stranger, more uncomfortable contradictions that come with being seen and treated as a woman. I'd genuinely love to hear if any of you have had similar experiences, because I think these are conversations worth having! The full video goes into far more depth on this whole experience. Premieres at 7:30 AM PST! I'll be live chatting, and as always, all my YouTube revenue goes to trans charities ❤️ https://youtu.be/vkKTx36FypI
